verdict: MedKayfab Pharmacology Core Edition drops 56 named characters that actually make the liver bear shred your textbooks into confetti. The naming system (Roxy Receptor, First Pass Frank, Cyp the CYP450 Chief) is the deck's killer feature—each name immediately embodies its mechanism with a visual punch that sticks like CYP3A4 to Simvastatin. Weakness: cards 30-31 (Anticholinesterase, Cholinergic Crisis Matrix) slide into reference-table mode rather than performance mode, and card 16's lore is truncated by the watermark. Table-ready: YES—mandatory material for any medical school pharmacology workshop.
blurb: 56 illustrated characters make pharmacology unforgettable—from First Pass Frank shredding your bioavailability to Poly Polypharmacy's donkey walking off a cliff. For medical students who need mechanisms that actually stick.

marketingText:
MedKayfab: PHARMACOLOGY CORE – The Rules Every Drug Obeys (Medical Mnemonics Cut & Play Comic)

56 illustrated medical mnemonic cards to master absorption and first-pass metabolism, the dose-response curve, and the enzyme interactions that turn two safe drugs into one disaster.

Here is the lie that gets first-years killed on the wards: that pharmacology is a memory contest, two hundred drug names against your flashcards, and whoever stacks the most cards wins. It is not. Every drug in that pile answers to the same short list of rules before it does anything useful. How much survives the first trip through the liver. Where the molecule hides once it is in. Whether one notch up the dose nudges the level or doubles it. Which enzyme some other pill just switched on or off. Learn the drug and skip the rule, and you will dose perfectly from memory and still watch the contraceptive fail, the statin dissolve a muscle, and the level climb on a dose you never changed.

MedKayfab Pharmacology Core turns the invisible grammar of absorption, distribution, and metabolism into a narrative wrestling match, where every rule that decides whether a drug heals or harms shows up as a character you have to out-think. Stop redrawing the curve from memory. Start arguing with the character who bends it.

YOU'LL GET
- 56 illustrated MedKayfab cards (15pp, 4 cards/page)
- Full MedKayfab Freestyle rules (Quest Die mechanics)
- S-Tier characters like Dose the Dose-Response, First Pass Frank, and Indie the Inducer
- Free lifetime updates as the pharmacology gets sharper
- CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence, print, share, and adapt freely
- PDF optimized for home printing (A4 / Letter)

What's in the deck
This deck personifies the rules layer, the physics every prescription obeys before a single brand name matters. You will meet First Pass Frank, the liver's bouncer who shreds most of an oral dose before it ever reaches the blood, the one reason a pill and a drip are not the same drug. Indie the Inducer works slower and meaner, quietly teaching the liver to chew through everything faster until the pill that mattered stops showing up to work. And Dose the Dose-Response holds the curve itself, keeper of the rule that potency is not efficacy, that the strongest-sounding drug is rarely the one that does the most. Around them sit Zero the Zero-Order, where one small step up the dose triggers a massive jump in level, and Poly Polypharmacy, whose donkey of stacked prescriptions walks the elderly straight off a cliff.

How it works
Every card is a cognitive anchor built for the moment you actually need it: the Character (the mnemonic), the Visual (the scene that makes it stick), the Stat Block (the numbers, the kinetics, the windows), the Lore (why the rule exists), and the Quest (a case where the rule is the whole answer). Mechanism Flash is the brutal mode: name the rule in one sentence without looking, predict what it does to the next dose, or the "patient" on the Stage pays for the pause.

Honest cognitive load
This is the foundation deck, the one to run first. It is built for preclinical and early-clinical students who keep getting blindsided by the same handful of principles, the ones that quietly underwrite every specialty exam and every ward round after. Difficulty is moderate and the load is conceptual rather than encyclopedic, which is the whole point. It pairs naturally with Essential Pharmacology for the drug classes and toxicities that ride on top of these rules, and with any clinical specialty deck where the rule finally cashes out at the bedside.

ABOUT MEDKAYFAB
MedKayfab is a narrative medical learning card game, 50 decks covering the full medical curriculum. Every card encodes a clinical mechanism as a character with a personality, a story, and a reasoning challenge. Built by a physician. Assembled with AI tools. Manually revised. Honest about its limitations. Free to use, share, and adapt under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

PAY WHAT YOU WANT
This deck is Pay What You Want, including free. If you find it useful, a fair price is €5. If you are a student on a budget, enter €0, no questions asked. If you want to support more decks, anything above fair price is appreciated. Share freely, attribute honestly, never resell.

DISCLAIMER
MedKayfab is a learning companion, not a clinical reference. Content was created by a physician and reviewed to the best of our knowledge, but medicine evolves, guidelines change, and some mechanisms in here will be simplified or wrong. Always verify against current primary sources and clinical guidelines before applying anything to patient care. The Blödsinn! is the vehicle. The science is serious.

Stay fluffy. — Doc FrizzleBob
